mock_data.title: Problems at Work
mock_data.passage:
A letter giving news of office politics and events.

4/6/01

Dear Sam,

I hope you're enjoying the course. You certainly chose a good time to be away from the office. I thought I'd better write and put you in the picture about what's been going on here in your absence. Forewarned is forearmed and you might decide not to bother coming back! Most of us are seriously thinking about leaving if things don't improve.

It all started when Mr Brown was taken ill suddenly. Apparently, he was at death's door for a while and everyone was very worried about him. However, the doctors eventually found out what was wrong. He's had an operation and he'll be up and about next week, although he won't be back in harness for a couple of months. And that's the problem.

Unfortunately for us in the office, Mr Brown's sister was visiting him from America when he was taken ill. She is now, as she puts it, at the helm while he's off work, and has installed herself in his office. When we first heard about it most of us weren't much bothered about it, although having someone brought in over him made the deputy manager hopping mad.

However, we had a swift change of attitude when we met Mrs Wiley, as she is called. She is 50 if she's a day and is definitely a case of mutton dressed as lamb. She must spend hours putting on her slap in the morning! Not that we care what age she is or what she looks like, but we care about how she treats us—and that is very badly.

She has her own business in New York and she's always telling us how much better her staff are than us. I bet they're all having a ball while she's away and hoping that she won't come back. It is impossible to please her and she criticizes everyone's work all the time. Mr Brown's secretary simply could not stand it any longer and is now off ill with stress. The rest of us are thinking of joining her!

When she arrived in the office her opening gambit was that we must all work very hard to ensure that the business did not suffer while the owner was away. It's suffering all right! No one likes her and we're losing both clients and suppliers.

See what I mean about staying away?

Best wishes
Billy

mock_data.passageC1:
Dear Sam,

I trust you’re reaping the benefits of your course. Your timing couldn't have been better, considering the current climate at the office. I felt compelled to bring you up to speed on the unfolding drama; a little forewarning might be prudent, perhaps even dissuading you from a premature return! To be frank, morale is so low that a significant number of us are contemplating tendering our resignations if the situation doesn't take a turn for the better.

The catalyst for this upheaval was, of course, Mr. Brown’s sudden illness. He was, by all accounts, touch and go for a while, causing considerable anxiety amongst the staff. Thankfully, the medical team identified the problem, and he's since undergone surgery. He’s expected to be back on his feet next week, although a return to the office is unlikely for a couple of months. And therein lies the rub.

Unfortunately, Mr. Brown’s sister happened to be visiting from the States when his health took a nosedive. She has now, rather presumptuously, appointed herself as the acting head, taking the reins during his absence and installing herself in his office. Initially, most of us were relatively unconcerned, although the deputy manager was visibly irked by this external appointment.

However, our indifference evaporated upon meeting Mrs. Wiley. She's easily 50, if not older, and undeniably a case of mutton dressed as lamb. One suspects she dedicates an inordinate amount of time to her morning makeup routine! However, her age and appearance are largely irrelevant; our primary concern lies with her appalling treatment of the staff.

She owns a business in New York and is constantly singing the praises of her employees, implying their superiority to us. I daresay they are thoroughly enjoying her absence and secretly hoping she won’t return. She is utterly impossible to satisfy and relentlessly criticizes everyone's work. Mr. Brown's secretary, unable to stomach the pressure any longer, is now on sick leave, suffering from stress. The rest of us are seriously considering following suit!

Upon her arrival, her opening spiel was that we must all work diligently to ensure the business doesn't suffer in the owner's absence. Quite the contrary! Morale is at rock bottom, and we're haemorrhaging both clients and suppliers.

Do you now understand my suggestion to extend your stay?

Best wishes,

Billy

Ofis siyosati va voqealar haqida xabar beruvchi xat.

4/6/01

Hurmatli Sam,

Umid qilamanki, kursdan zavqlanayotgandirsan. Sen ofisdan uzoqda bo'lish uchun juda yaxshi vaqtni tanladingiz. Men senga bu yerda yo'qligingda nima bo'layotgani haqida yozib, vaziyatni tushuntirishim kerak deb o'yladim. Oldindan ogohlantirish - qurolanmoqdir va sen qaytib kelmaslikka qaror qilishing mumkin! Agar vaziyat yaxshilanmasa, ko'pchiligimiz ketish haqida jiddiy o'ylayapmiz.

Hammasi janob Braun to'satdan kasal bo'lganida boshlandi. Ko'rinishidan, u bir muddat o'lim yoqasida edi va hamma u haqida juda xavotir bo'ldi. Biroq, shifokorlar oxir-oqibat nima bo'lganini aniqladilar. U operatsiya qildi va kelasi hafta oyoqqa turib, yura boshlaydi, garchi u bir-ikki oyga ishga qaytmaydi. Va muammo shu yerda.

Afsuski, biz uchun, janob Braunning singlisi u kasallanganida uni ko'rish uchun Amerikadan kelgan edi. U hozir, o'zi aytganidek, u ishlamayotgan paytda rahbarlik o'rnida va uning kabinetiga joylashgan. Biz bu haqda birinchi marta eshitganimizda, ko'pchiligimiz bu haqda ko'p tashvishlanmadik, garchi uning ustiga birovni olib kelish o'rinbosar menejerni juda g'azablantirdi.

Biroq, biz Missis Uayli bilan uchrashganimizda fikrimiz tez o'zgardi. U kamida 50 yoshda va u aniq "qo'y terisidagi qo'chqor" - ya'ni yoshroq ko'rinishga harakat qilayotgan keksa ayol. U ertalab soatlab pardoz qiladi! Bizni uning yoshi yoki qanday ko'rinishi qiziqtirmaydi, lekin bizga qanday munosabatda bo'lishi muhim - va bu juda yomon.

Uning Nyu-Yorkda o'z biznesi bor va u doimo bizga o'z xodimlari bizdan qanchalik yaxshiroq ekanligini aytadi. Men ishonchim komilki, u yo'q paytda ular hammasi zavqlanishyapti va uning qaytmaslgini umid qilishyapti. Uni mamnun qilish imkonsiz va u doimo hammaning ishini tanqid qiladi. Janob Braunning kotibi boshqa chidab turolmadi va hozir stress sababli kasallanib uyda. Qolganlarmiz ham unga qo'shilish haqida o'ylayapmiz!

U ofisga kelganida uning dastlabki harakati shunday ediki, egasi yo'q paytda biznes zarar ko'rmasligi uchun hammamiz juda qattiq ishlashimiz kerak. U zarar ko'ryapti, albatta! Hech kim uni yoqtirmaydi va biz mijozlarni ham, yetkazib beruvchilarni ham yo'qotayapmiz.

Uzoqda qolish haqida nima demoqchi ekanligimni tushundingmi?

Eng yaxshi tilaklar bilan
Billi

Salom, Sem!

Umid qilamanki, kursdan rohatlanyapsan. Ofisdan uzoqda bo'lish uchun yaxshi vaqtni tanlading. Senga xat yozib, sen yo'qligingda bu yerda nima bo'layotganini aytmoqchi edim. Tayyor bo'lgan yaxshi, balki qaytishni ham xohlamassan! Agar vaziyat yaxshilanmasa, ko'pchiligimiz ketish haqida o'ylayapmiz.

Hamma narsa janob Braunning to'satdan kasal bo'lib qolishidan boshlandi. U bir muddat juda og'ir ahvolda edi va hamma xavotirda edi. Ammo shifokorlar nimasi noto'g'ri ekanligini aniqlashdi. U operatsiya qilindi va tez orada tuzalib ketadi, lekin u bir necha oy ishga qaytmaydi. Va muammo ham shunda.
